_comment: Press stories about astronauts on PR duty (design.md 2.2(c)). '{name}' is the astronaut's name. 'tone' GOOD pays a bonus, BAD costs prestige. Optional 'effects' do more: each has a 'kind' (PrPress.EffectKind says what 'target', 'amount' and 'seasons' mean for it). Stories must read for either agency and any astronaut: no pronouns, no country-specific terms, nothing the rules don't model, and nothing that can't happen twice. A few are nods to real events, listed in design.md 1.1. Ids are stored in turn reports: never rename or reuse one.

stories.headline: {name}'s three-word speech
stories.text: Asked for a few words at the rocket plant, {name} says only "Do good work." By the end of the week the workers have painted it on banners above the assembly line.

stories.headline: {name} raises both hands
stories.text: Asked at a press conference who expects to come back from space, every astronaut raises a hand. {name} raises two, and that photo makes every front page.

stories.headline: {name} rides through the rain
stories.text: Offered a closed car in a downpour, {name} insists on the open one: if the crowds can stand in the rain, so can their guest. The soaked photos win the city over.

stories.headline: The walk the whole country watched
stories.text: Newsreels of {name}'s long walk down the red carpet show something flapping loose at one ankle the whole way. Viewers love it: their hero is one of them.

stories.headline: A puppy from {name}
stories.text: {name} presents a puppy to a visiting leader's children. The agency's post room is buried under thousands of letters asking for one from the next litter.

stories.headline: {name}'s family on the cover
stories.text: A glossy magazine puts {name}'s family on its cover, with a long story about life at home. The issue sells out, and the editors ask for more.

stories.headline: {name}'s paintings on stamps
stories.text: {name} paints space scenes in spare hours, and the post office prints a set of them as stamps. Collectors queue round the block.

stories.headline: {name} visits a village school
stories.text: {name} spends an afternoon answering children's questions, the best being whether the Moon smells of anything. The teachers report a rush to join the science club.

stories.headline: {name} answers every letter
stories.text: Word gets out that {name} replies to fan mail by hand, often late into the night. Sacks of new letters arrive on the next train.

stories.headline: Newborns named after {name}
stories.text: Registry offices report a run of babies named after {name}. One proud father brings twins to the next public appearance.

stories.headline: {name} on the night shift
stories.text: At a steelworks, {name} swaps the dress uniform for a hard hat and spends an hour with the night shift. The workers' newspaper prints the whole visit.

stories.headline: {name} wins a quiz for charity
stories.text: On a television quiz, {name} sweeps the science round and gives the prize money to a children's hospital.

stories.headline: Crowds close a runway for {name}
stories.text: So many people come to meet {name}'s plane that the airport closes a runway for an hour. The pictures run for days.

stories.headline: {name} drives a harvester
stories.text: At a harvest festival, {name} takes a turn on a combine harvester and cuts a dead straight row. Farmers who never cared about rockets now do.

stories.headline: {name} salutes the old pilots
stories.text: {name} spends a day with veteran wartime aviators, listening far more than talking. Their association writes to the papers in praise.

stories.headline: Stuck in a lift with {name}
stories.text: A hotel lift stalls for forty minutes with {name} and six strangers inside. All six give glowing interviews the next morning.

stories.headline: A night under the stars
stories.text: {name} leads a public evening at an observatory, pointing out the planets one by one. Thousands come, and the queue reaches the car park.

stories.headline: {name} at the children's ward
stories.text: {name} quietly visits a children's hospital, with no cameras invited. A nurse's letter to the paper tells the story anyway.

stories.headline: Model rockets with {name}
stories.text: {name} judges a model rocket contest and launches the winning entry. Toy shops sell out of kits within the week.

stories.headline: A warm welcome abroad
stories.text: On a tour abroad, {name} greets the crowd in its own language: a few practised sentences that bring the house down.

stories.headline: {name} kicks off the cup final
stories.text: {name} takes the ceremonial first kick at a packed stadium and gets a standing ovation from both ends.

stories.headline: {name} credits the engineers
stories.text: Asked about courage, {name} talks for ten minutes about the engineers and technicians instead. Their families cut the article out and pin it up at home.

stories.headline: Applications soar after {name}'s tour
stories.text: Engineering colleges report a jump in applications from every town {name} visited this season.

stories.headline: {name} takes the listeners' calls
stories.text: A late-night radio call-in with {name} runs two hours over time. The switchboard never stops lighting up.

stories.headline: {name} charms the budget committee
stories.text: The people who set the agency's budget spend a day touring with {name}. They leave asking what the agency could do with a little more money.

stories.headline: An engineer writes to {name}
stories.text: A fan letter to {name} from a brilliant engineer ends with a job application, and the SET Centre wants to meet them at once.

stories.headline: {name} stars in a supplier's adverts
stories.text: A supplier pays the agency well to put {name} in its adverts. The money is welcome; {name} hates every minute of the shoot.

stories.headline: {name}'s holiday mishap
stories.text: {name} turns up after a seaside holiday with stitches over one eyebrow and a story about a balcony that nobody believes. The rumours do the rest.

stories.headline: {name} slips at home
stories.text: Fixing a bathroom mirror, {name} slips and hits the tub, and spends the season's appearances dizzy and unsteady. The papers have fun with the astronaut who can't stand up straight.

stories.headline: {name} argues with a patrol
stories.text: A late evening ends with {name} arguing with a military patrol at a railway station, then refusing to apologise. The report travels up the chain of command.

stories.headline: {name} never arrives
stories.text: A delayed train leaves a full hall waiting for {name}, who never shows up. The local paper's headline is not kind.

stories.headline: {name}'s shiny new car
stories.text: {name} is photographed in a gleaming sports car, a gift from a dealer. Readers start asking what astronauts are paid, and why so much.

stories.headline: {name} stopped for speeding
stories.text: A police officer pulls {name} over at twice the limit on a country road. The officer is not impressed by the offer of an autograph.

stories.headline: {name} says too much
stories.text: In an unguarded moment, {name} tells reporters about a test that hasn't happened yet. The agency spends the week denying it.

stories.headline: {name} nods off on stage
stories.text: Worn out by the tour, {name} falls asleep during a mayor's long speech, and a photographer catches the moment.

stories.headline: {name} walks out
stories.text: Asked once too often about the dangers, {name} walks out of a press conference. The empty chair makes the front page.

stories.headline: {name} cashing in
stories.text: Badges and mugs with {name}'s face turn up in every kiosk, licensed without the agency's say. The papers call it cashing in.

stories.headline: {name} thanks the wrong town
stories.text: {name} warmly thanks the people of the next town over, to a crowd that does not laugh.

stories.headline: A photographer follows {name} in
stories.text: A press photographer slips into the plant behind {name}'s party and snaps a component on the test bench. The team loses a season to security checks and paperwork.
